description: HungerCount is the national count of food bank use in Canada, taken over one month each year across the food bank network. It is run by Food Banks Canada, the national association of food banks, and published as an annual report. The 2025 edition covers 2,725 reporting food banks and records nearly 2.2 million visits in the survey month, double the 2019 level, together with meals and snacks served. Results are given for Canada and each province and territory, with the share of visits by children, and client profiles by age, income source, household type and housing, including people in temporary shelters. The figures are available free on the web pages for each province and territory, and the full report is available to download as a PDF. Caveats: the count covers a single month a year, depends on food banks responding, and is not published as a machine-readable table, so values must be transcribed. Simulation uses: sizing the throughput and client load of food bank networks, and setting baseline demand for emergency food distribution after disasters. Related records: Statistics Canada food insecurity (data-statcan-food-insecurity-by-family-type) measures the wider population at risk, and Map the Meal Gap (data-feeding-america-map-the-meal-gap) is the US counterpart for local food need.

schema_summary: Per province or territory and Canada for the survey month: total visits, child visits, percentage change from the previous year and from 2019, meals and snacks served, number of food banks reporting; client shares by age group, primary source of income, household type, housing type and other demographic groups

sources.note: HungerCount 2025: nearly 2.2 million visits in a single month, double six years earlier; Canada total visits 2,165,776, child visits 711,770, change 2024-2025 5.15%, change 2019-2025 99.37%, meals and snacks 4,522,356, food banks reporting 2,725; provincial and territorial data selectable; methodology and full report download

User statistics for Canada: shares by age group, primary source of income, household type, housing type (market rental 70.4%, unhoused or temporary shelters 6.3%) and other demographic information; racialized communities question added in 2021

temporal_coverage: Annual survey (2025 edition compared with 2019 onwards)
